HomePage.title: PairSight
HomePage.tagline: A second look at every match.
HomePage.description: Compare entity-resolution vendors on your own customer records. PairSight asks Jev to judge each candidate pair, then shows where each vendor agrees or disagrees.
HomePage.stepUpload: Upload your records and each vendor’s matches
HomePage.stepRules: Choose which pairs are worth checking
HomePage.stepCompare: See where vendors and PairSight disagree

Auth.signInDescription: Your evaluations are saved to your account.
Auth.signUpDescription: Save evaluations and come back to them later.
Auth.invalidInput: Enter a valid email and a password of at least {min} characters.
Auth.checkEmail: Check your email to confirm your account, then sign in.

Evaluations.title: Evaluations
Evaluations.description: Each evaluation compares one set of source records against one or more vendors’ matches.
Evaluations.emptyDescription: An evaluation compares one set of your records against each vendor’s matches. Name one above, then upload your files.
Evaluations.runSummary: Run {number} · {pairs, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}}

Records.title: Source records
Records.description: Upload the CSV every vendor evaluated. Each row needs a unique record reference.
Records.replaceWarning: Replacing the source file starts a new dataset. Vendor results must be uploaded again, and earlier runs keep their original records.
Records.dropHint: Drop the CSV every vendor evaluated, or choose it. A header row, up to 500 records and 1 MB.
Records.previewDescription: Pick the column that uniquely identifies each record, then tell PairSight what each column contains. Suggestions come from the column names — check them.
Records.saved: Saved {count, plural, one {# record} other {# records}}.
Records.missingReferences: {count, plural, one {# row has} other {# rows have}} no record reference: {rows}
Records.duplicateRoles: Each role can be mapped to one column only. Used more than once: {roles}

CsvErrors.empty: The file has no data rows under the header.
CsvErrors.too_many_rows: The file has {found} rows; the limit is {limit}.
CsvErrors.too_many_columns: The file has {found} columns; the limit is {limit}.
CsvErrors.duplicate_header: More than one column is named: {headers}
CsvErrors.ragged_rows: These rows have a different number of cells than the header: {rows}
CsvErrors.too_large: The file is larger than 1 MB.

Vendors.title: Vendor results
Vendors.description: Upload each vendor’s export of the pairs it matched. Vendor names, scores and decisions are never sent to Jev.
Vendors.added: {count, plural, one {# matched pair} other {# matched pairs}}
Vendors.completeTitle: Is this the vendor’s complete list of matches?
Vendors.completeExplanation: PairSight treats any pair missing from this file as “not matched” by the vendor. That’s only fair if the export lists every match the vendor made on these same records.
Vendors.completeConfirm: Yes, this export lists every match this vendor made
Vendors.savedSummary: Added {pairs, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}}. {skipped}
Vendors.skipped: {self, plural, =0 {} one {# self-pair skipped.} other {# self-pairs skipped.}} {duplicates, plural, =0 {} one {# repeated row collapsed.} other {# repeated rows collapsed.}}
Vendors.unknownReferences: {count, plural, one {# reference isn’t} other {# references aren’t}} in the source records
Vendors.missingReferenceRows: {count, plural, one {# row is} other {# rows are}} missing a reference: {rows}
Vendors.maxVendors: You can compare up to {max} vendors.
Vendors.errorsTitle: Fix these before adding this vendor
Vendors.dropHint: Drop the vendor’s export, or choose it: one matched pair per row, with two record-reference columns.

Rules.title: Identity and blocking
Rules.description: Define what counts as the same person, then choose which pairs are worth asking Jev about.
Rules.identityTitle: What counts as the same individual
Rules.countryHint: Two-letter code, used to read local phone numbers
Rules.jevFieldsDescription: Only these mapped fields are sent, together with your definition above.
Rules.blockingDescription: Records that share a value under any rule become candidate pairs. Rules overlap, and blocking never decides a match — Jev does.
Rules.ruleEmailHint: Trimmed and lowercased; dots and +tags kept
Rules.rulePhoneHint: Converted to international format using the country
Rules.ruleNameHint: Case, spacing and full vs. first + last name normalized
Rules.stats: {buckets, plural, one {# group} other {# groups}} · {pairs, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}} · largest {largest}
Rules.bucketWarning: A group of {size, number} records creates {pairs, number} pairs. This only affects workload, not accuracy.
Rules.countryUnsaved: Unsaved change: the counts below still read phone numbers as {country}. Save to recount them with the new country.
Rules.ruleOverCap: This rule alone creates {pairs, number} pairs; one run allows {limit, number}.
Rules.customHint: Custom rule: every field must match
Rules.customDescription: Pick up to three fields. Records become a candidate pair only when all of them match after normalization.
Rules.customDuplicate: A rule with these fields already exists.
Rules.customLimit: You can add up to {max} custom rules.

Plan.title: Review the plan
Plan.description: This is exactly what the run will evaluate. Nothing is sent to Jev until you start.
Plan.addedByVendor: Added only because a vendor matched them
Plan.reusable: Already judged in an earlier run (reused)
Plan.jevReceives: For each pair: {fields}, your definition of the same individual, and the country. No vendor names, scores or decisions, and no record references.
Plan.cost: Estimated cost: about {cost} (at a stand-in rate until TypeSafe publishes its own price).
Plan.fictionalOnly: Use fictional or anonymized records only for now.
Plan.no_vendors: Add at least one vendor’s results.
Plan.no_jev_fields: Choose at least one field for Jev to compare.
Plan.no_pairs: There are no pairs to evaluate. Turn on a blocking rule or add vendor results.
Plan.too_many_pairs: This plan has {count} pairs; one run allows {limit}.
Plan.causeVendors: Added only because a vendor matched them: {pairs} pairs
Plan.causesNote: Rules overlap, so these can add up to more than the total.
Plan.fixRules: Turn off or narrow a rule

Run.title: Run {number}
Run.description: Jev assesses each planned pair using only the fields you selected.
Run.metaRunning: Finished assessments are saved as they arrive.
Run.metaStopped: Resume to continue where it stopped. Finished assessments are saved.
Run.errorUnknown: The run couldn’t continue. Try again in a moment.
Run.incompleteTitle: {count, plural, one {# assessment is} other {# assessments are}} incomplete.
Run.incompleteBody: They appear as Incomplete in results, are excluded from metrics, and never count as nonmatches.
Run.stoppedNote: No more pairs are sent until you resume. Finished assessments are saved.
Run.noteLeave: Leaving this page pauses processing. Your progress is saved, and the run picks up where it stopped when you come back.
Run.noteIncomplete: Incomplete assessments never become nonmatches — they stay Incomplete until assessed.

Categories.both_matchedMeaning: Vendor and PairSight agree it’s a match
Categories.pairsight_onlyMeaning: A possible duplicate the vendor missed
Categories.vendor_onlyMeaning: A possible wrong vendor match — or a PairSight mistake
Categories.incompleteMeaning: Not judged yet, or the evaluation failed

Results.title: Results
Results.agreementNote: Categories show agreement between the vendor and PairSight, not proven correctness.
Results.coverage: {total, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}} compared — {fromRules} from your rules, {addedByVendor} added only because a vendor matched them.
Results.incompleteBanner: {percent}% judged — {count, plural, one {# pair is} other {# pairs are}} incomplete and excluded from the four categories.
Results.thresholdHelp: Pairs Jev scores at or above this count as a PairSight match. Changing it re-reads saved scores — no new AI calls.
Results.noResultsHint: Try another category or score range, or clear filters to see every planned pair.
Results.noPairsHint: Nothing was compared for this vendor in this run. Check the run’s progress, or start a new run from the plan.
Results.distributionTitle: How Jev scored the judged pairs
Results.distributionSummary: {above, plural, one {# pair scores} other {# pairs score}} at or above {threshold}, {below} below.
Results.previewNoChange: No pair changes category at this threshold.
Results.coverageHowRules: PairSight compares the pairs your blocking rules find, plus every pair a vendor matched even when your rules didn’t find it.
Results.coverageHowBlindSpot: Pairs outside your rules that no vendor matched weren’t evaluated, so duplicates that every vendor missed among them can’t be seen here.
Results.tableCaption: Planned pairs. Use the arrow keys to move between rows and Enter to inspect a pair.
Results.thresholdSetDescription: Decisions updated from saved scores. No new Jev assessments were made.

Pair.aiNote: AI judgment — it may be wrong. Jev returned a score only; no explanation is available for this pair.
Pair.pendingJudgment: Jev hasn’t judged this pair yet.
Pair.failedJudgment: Jev couldn’t judge this pair ({reason}). It’s excluded from the categories until it’s judged.
Pair.originVendor: Added because {vendors} matched it. It falls outside your rules, so it was only compared because a vendor matched it.
Pair.keyboardHint: <key>J</key> <key>K</key> next and previous · <key>Esc</key> back to results
Pair.retryError: Jev couldn’t judge it this time either. Try again in a moment.
Pair.incompleteNote: Excluded from metrics. An incomplete assessment never counts as “no match”.
Pair.scoreBarLabel: Score {score} on a 0 to 1 scale. Threshold {threshold}.
Pair.originNote: Vendor decisions are never sent to Jev — it only sees the record fields used for assessment.

Unsaved.title: Leave without saving?
Unsaved.description: Your changes to the identity definition, Jev fields or blocking rules haven’t been saved. If you leave now, they’ll be lost.

Pipeline.runDone: Run {number} · {pairs, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}}

Welcome.title: Welcome to PairSight
Welcome.description: One thing before you start: what should we call you?
Welcome.nameHint: Shown on your account. You can use any name you like.

Overview.provisionalNote: {count, plural, one {# planned pair is} other {# planned pairs are}} still incomplete and excluded. Metrics may change when they’re assessed.
Overview.precisionTip: Of the pairs {vendor} matched, the share Jev also judged the same individual. Low precision means wrong merges.
Overview.recallTip: Of the pairs Jev judged the same individual, the share {vendor} also matched. Low recall means missed duplicates.
Overview.f1Tip: The harmonic mean of precision and recall. A summary of the tradeoff — not overall accuracy.
Overview.precisionMeaning: {count, plural, one {# merge} other {# merges}} judged as different people
Overview.recallMeaning: {count, plural, one {# likely duplicate} other {# likely duplicates}} not matched
Overview.f1Meaning: Not a measure of overall accuracy
Overview.coverageHowRules: Your rules chose <n>{fromRules}</n> pairs worth comparing. Every pair any vendor matched was added too — <n>{added}</n> of those fell outside your rules.
Overview.coverageHowBlindSpot: The other <n>{notCompared}</n> possible pairs were never compared. If duplicates hide among them, neither PairSight nor this report can see them, so recall describes evaluated pairs only.
Overview.coverageFootnote: Duplicates among pairs outside your rules can’t be seen. Recall applies to evaluated pairs only.
Overview.categoryTileLabel: {category}: {count, plural, one {# pair} other {# pairs}}. Show these pairs

meaning.both_matched: {vendor} and PairSight both judged these the same individual

Overview.incompleteMeaning: <n>{pending}</n> pending · <n>{failed}</n> failed. Excluded from metrics — never counted as no match.
Overview.sectionDecisionsHint: How decisions line up, and how robust they are
Overview.sectionDisagreementsHint: Patterns worth checking before you trust a vendor’s merges
Overview.matrixDescription: {vendor} decisions against PairSight decisions · {assessed} assessed pairs
Overview.sensitivityDescription: How {vendor}’s metrics move as the PairSight threshold changes · saved scores only
Overview.sensitivityChartLabel: Precision, recall and F1 across thresholds. At the current threshold {threshold}: precision {precision}, recall {recall}.
Overview.comparisonDescription: Same assessed pairs, same reference · fixed 0–100% scale
Overview.comparisonChartLabel: Precision, recall and F1 per vendor. {summary}
Overview.tradeoffBoth: {vendor} is higher on both precision and recall for these evaluated pairs.
Overview.tradeoffSplit: {precise} makes fewer wrong merges (precision); {recall} finds more duplicates (recall). Which matters more depends on what a wrong merge costs you versus a missed one.
Overview.overlapDescription: Assessed pairs grouped by which vendors matched them
Overview.overlapExtra: {vendor}’s extra matches: {same} of {total} judged the same individual by Jev.
Overview.overlapMissedByBoth: {count, plural, one {# likely duplicate was} other {# likely duplicates were}} missed by both vendors.
Overview.overlapAgree: When both vendors agree, {percent}% are judged the same individual.
Overview.patternsTitle: What each category has in common
Overview.patternsInfo: Share of pairs in each category where both records hold the same value for a field. Pairs where either value is missing are left out of that cell.
Overview.patternsDescription: Field agreement between the two records, by category
Overview.patternsCaption: Share of pairs with the same field value, by category
Overview.patternMissed: PairSight-only pairs usually share {shared} — likely variants {vendor} didn’t link.
Overview.patternMissedDiffer: PairSight-only pairs usually share {shared} but differ on {different} — likely variants {vendor} didn’t link.
Overview.patternMerged: Vendor-only pairs mostly share {shared} — check for households or shared contact details.
Overview.patternMergedDiffer: Vendor-only pairs mostly share {shared} while {different} differ — check for households or shared contact details.
Overview.topDescription: The disagreements where Jev’s score is furthest from the vendor’s decision
Overview.sourcesDescription: Which rules surfaced each kind of pair
Overview.sourcesFootnote: A pair found by several rules counts once under each. “Added by a vendor” pairs sit outside every rule.
Overview.workloadNearDetail: Scores within ±0.10 — most sensitive to the threshold
